seoTitle: How to Connect Walmart to Shopify (Sell on Walmart)
metaDescription: Sell your Shopify products on Walmart Marketplace by installing a Walmart connector app, linking your seller account, syncing products, and managing orders.
intro: Walmart Marketplace puts your products in front of shoppers who will never find your standalone Shopify store, and you don't need a second inventory system to get there. A connector app bridges the two platforms so your catalog, stock levels, and orders stay in one place. This guide walks through installing that connector from the Shopify App Store, reviewing what access it needs, and what happens once your seller account is linked — the exact steps shown in the video, with the real screens you'll click through.

steps.heading: Search the Shopify App Store for a Walmart connector
steps.body: From your Shopify admin, open the App Store and type "walmart" into the search bar. Shopify's autocomplete will surface related searches like carrier names and category filters such as Sales channels and Selling products before you even finish typing — useful if you want to browse rather than search directly. Several apps handle the Walmart connection; the video uses CedCommerce Walmart Connector, one of the more established options with real store reviews behind it.

image.caption: Searching "walmart" in the Shopify App Store, with Shopify's autocomplete suggesting related carriers and app categories.

steps.heading: Review what the app actually does
steps.body: Before installing anything that touches your product and order data, open the app's listing page and read what it claims to handle. CedCommerce's listing describes real-time catalog and inventory syncing, bulk product management, optional use of Walmart's own fulfillment network, and a repricer tool that auto-adjusts your prices to stay competitive. It's free to install with a free trial, which matters if you just want to test the connection before committing to a paid tier. Skimming this page tells you whether the app matches what you actually need — some sellers only want catalog sync, others want Walmart to handle fulfillment too, and the feature list is where that gets decided.

image.caption: The CedCommerce Walmart Connector listing page, showing its pricing, feature list, and that it works specifically with Walmart.com.

steps.heading: Install the app and approve its permissions
steps.body: Clicking Install brings up a permissions screen listing exactly what the app can see and change: personal data like customers and store owner details, and store data including products and orders. This is the point to actually read the list rather than click through it, since a Walmart connector legitimately needs product and order access to do its job, but you should still know that's what you're granting. Confirming here installs the app into your Shopify admin, where it'll appear in your apps list for every future session.

image.caption: The install permissions screen for CedCommerce Walmart Connector, listing access to customer data and to product and order data.

steps.heading: Connect your Walmart Seller account
steps.body: Once installed, the app walks you through linking your Walmart Seller Center account, which typically means authenticating with the API credentials or login Walmart issues to approved sellers. You need an approved Walmart Marketplace seller account before this step works — the connector links two existing accounts, it doesn't create a Walmart seller profile for you. If you haven't applied to sell on Walmart Marketplace yet, that application needs to clear first.

steps.heading: Sync your product catalog
steps.body: With accounts linked, the app can push your Shopify products to Walmart, mapping titles, images, pricing, and variants into the format Walmart's catalog expects. Review the mapped listings before they go live, since Walmart has its own category and item-spec requirements that don't always translate one-to-one from a Shopify product page. Getting this right the first time saves you from a batch of rejected or mismatched listings later.

steps.heading: Manage Walmart orders from your Shopify admin
steps.body: Once products are live and selling, Walmart orders flow back into the same admin you already use for Shopify orders, so fulfillment doesn't mean switching between two dashboards all day. This is the real payoff of the integration: one order queue, one inventory count, and one place to update tracking, instead of manually reconciling two separate systems every time something sells.

faq.question: Do I need a separate Walmart Seller account?
faq.answer: Yes, you need an approved Walmart Marketplace Seller account before you can connect it to Shopify. The connector app links two existing accounts; it can't create a Walmart seller profile for you.

faq.question: Is the Walmart integration app free?
faq.answer: Pricing varies by app. CedCommerce Walmart Connector, shown in this guide, is free to install with a free trial, though ongoing use of some features may move to a paid tier.

faq.question: Will inventory stay in sync between Walmart and Shopify?
faq.answer: Yes, most integration apps sync inventory levels automatically so stock counts stay accurate across both platforms once your catalog is mapped and synced.

faq.question: Can I fulfill Walmart orders the same way as Shopify orders?
faq.answer: Yes, once synced, Walmart orders appear in your Shopify admin alongside your regular orders and can be fulfilled using your normal fulfillment process.
